question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- \frac{x^{6}}{8} + \frac{7 x^{3}}{4} + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=- \frac{3 x^{5}}{4} + \frac{21 x^{2}}{4}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=- \frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} + \frac{21 \left(2\right)^{2}}{4}=-3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-3\right)}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(7\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3}+\left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(7\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3} + \frac{19}{3}\\
\left(-3\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(-21\right)\\
x+\left(-3\right)y&=-19
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-3$ and the constant is $-19$.

\left(8\right)y&=-x+\left(1\right)+\left(48\right)\\

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=- \frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} + \frac{21 \left(2\right)^{2}}{4}=-3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-3\right)}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(4\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\

\end{aligned}

The coefficient is $-3$ and the constant is $-10$.
